latest_substantive_result.summary: The intake adds three scoped Gaussian-constraint results. A uniform lower bound on the R-th singular value gives an ideal exact Student-t-envelope sampler for the residual/delta-conditioned law with a separate nonlinear-energy cost. A native collective-stable-rank certificate gives a different ideal exact envelope and a source-stated finite-output W1 theorem for homogeneous zero targets; the preserved implementation handles only one fixed dense rational input. A harmonic Gauss-law dual reduces exactly to a Weyl eigenvalue density whose normalizer is finite iff real D>1+1/k, so the D=2 target exists at every finite gauge rank without an established efficient large-k sampler. No historic-scale breakthrough is established. Final deterministic package and static-access checks passed; this adds no mathematical verification.
